Pradhan Mantri Kisan Urja Suraksha evam Utthaan Mahabhiyan (KUSUM) Scheme  Launch: 2019  Nodal Ministry: Ministry of New & Renewable Energy  Objectives: o De-dieselisation of farm sector o Providing water and energy security to farmers o Increasing income of farmers o Curbing environmental pollution  Tenure: Till 31.3.2026  Central Financial Support: ₹34,422 Crore  Target: Solar capacity addition of 34,800 MW by March 2026

# Page 4^page=4
Components  Component A: Setting up of 10,000 MW of Decentralized Ground/ Stilt Mounted Grid Connected Solar or other Renewable Energy based Power Plants by farmers on their land o Solar or other Renewable Energy based Power Plants (REPP) of capacity of 500 kW to 2 MW will be setup by Renewable Power Generator (RPG) o REPP preferably installed within 5 km radius of sub-stations o Eligibility:  REPP would be installed by farmers on his own land either directly by himself or in partnership with group of farmers/ cooperatives/ panchayats/ Farmer Producer Organisations (FPO)/Water User associations (WUA)  Or through a developer  Farmer may provide (lease) his land to DISCOM  Power Purchase Agreement (PPA) of 25 years to be executed between RPG and Distribution Companies (DISCOMs)  Solar power generated will be purchased by DISCOMs at a feed-in-tariff (FiT) determined by respective State Electricity Regulatory Commission (SERC)  DISCOM would be eligible to get Procurement Based Incentive (PBI) @ ₹0.40 per unit purchased or ₹6.6 lakh per MW of capacity installed, whichever is less for 5 years from Commercial Operation Date (COD)

# Page 5^page=5
 Component B: Installation of 14 lakh standalone solar agricultural pumps o Individual farmers supported to install standalone Solar Agriculture pumps (of capacity up to 7.5 HP) or replacement of existing diesel Agriculture pumps / irrigation systems  in off-grid areas, where grid supply is not available o Existing standalone diesel pumps to be covered provided they use micro irrigation techniques o Priority given to small and marginal farmers and farmers using micro irrigation o Pumps of capacity higher than 7.5 HP may be allowed, but Central Financial Assistance (CFA) limited to CFA applicable for pump of 7.5 HP o For individual farmers in:  North-Eastern region (NER), Hilly region (Jammu & Kashmir, Ladakh, Uttarakhand, Himachal Pradesh), Island territories (Andaman & Nicobar, Lakshadweep)  CFA will be available for pump capacity up to 15 HP – restricted to 10% of total installations

# Page 6^page=6
o Implementation in 2 modes  Central Government provides financial assistance of 30% (or 50% for North Eastern Region/Hilly region/Islands)  State Government provides subsidy of at least 30%; and remaining up to 40% is to be provided by bank loan/farmer o If State Govt is not giving its share of subsidy of 30% but farmers are willing to set up solar water pumping system with Central Financial Assistance only:  Central share will remain 30% (or 50%), with remaining 70% in General category states and 50% in Hilly region/NER/Islands being borne by farmer o Through Universal Solar Pump Controller (USPC)  Farmers can use solar power for other activities like operating chaff cutter, floor mill, cold storage, drier, etc., and increase his income o New Solar Agriculture pumps would not be covered under this component in Dark zones/black zones of water o For solar pumps to be set up and used by  Water User Associations (WUA)/Farmer Producer Organizations (FPO)/Primary Agriculture Credit Societies (PACS) or for cluster-based irrigation system  CFA will be allowed for solar pump capacity of higher than 7.5 HP considering up to 7.5 HP capacity per individual in group

# Page 7^page=7
 Component C: Solarization of 35 lakh Grid Connected Agriculture pumps including Feeder Level Solarization o Feeder Level Solarization  Objective To provide reliable day-time solar power to farmers Enhancing farmers income by purchasing surplus solar power Thus incentivizing them for saving water  Applicable to farmers already connected to grid  CFA of 30% (50% in case of NE States, hilly states/UTs and Island UTs), balance will be met through loan from NABARD/PFC/REC  CFA of ₹1.05 Crore per MW  Can be implemented in CAPEX or RESCO (Renewable Energy Service Company) mode o Individual Pump Solarization (IPS)  2 Options: Pump to run on both Solar and Grid Pump to run on solar power only  CFA – same as Component B

# Page 8^page=8
Key Features  Allows transfer of quantities between Component-B and Component-C  Solarization of pumps under Component B & C of Scheme included under Agriculture Infrastructure Fund (AIF) to provide subsidized loans to farmers  Demand driven, therefore capacities are allocated based on demand received from states/UTs  Will help in stable and continuous source of income to rural land owners for a period of 25 years by utilisation of their land  Solarisation of agriculture pumps - under priority sector lending of RBI

# Page 10^page=10
Q. With reference to the PM-KUSUM Scheme, consider the following statements: 1. Under Component A, solar power plants are to be set up by Renewable Power Generators (RPGs) within a radius of 10 km from sub-stations. 2. DISCOMs are eligible for a Procurement Based Incentive (PBI) of ₹0.40 per unit purchased or ₹6.6 lakh per MW of capacity installed, whichever is higher, for 5 years from Commercial Operation Date. 3. In Component B, for farmers in North-Eastern and hilly states, Central Financial Assistance (CFA) is provided up to 50%, while in general category states it is limited to 30%. 4. Under Component C, feeder-level solarization aims at providing reliable day-time solar power to farmers and incentivizing water conservation by allowing surplus solar power sale. 5. The scheme allows transfer of quantities between Component B and Component C, based on demand received from states/UTs. Which of the above statements are correct? A. 3, 4 and 5 only B. 2 and 5 only C. 3, 4 and 5 only D. 4 and 5 only E. 3 and 4 only

Q. Consider the following statements regarding the Multidisciplinary Education and Research Improvement in Technical Education (MERITE) Scheme: 1. MERITE is a Centrally Sponsored Scheme with financial outlay of ₹4,200 crore. 2. Out of the total outlay, ₹2,100 crore will come as external assistance from the World Bank. 3. The scheme will cover 275 technical institutions, including engineering colleges and polytechnics across all States/UTs. 4. The interventions under the scheme are aligned with the National Education Policy (NEP), 2020. Which of the above statements is/are correct? A. 1 and 2 only B. 2, 3 and 4 only C. 1, 3 and 4 only D. 2 and 4 only E. 1, 2, 3 and 4 Answer: Option B
